system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
## Executive view

The Seller’s package departs materially from the Buyer’s playbook. The “standard/cleared” labels and efficiency note have no effect on Wattlebridge’s positions and should not be accepted as limiting the review.

## Key pushbacks

| Issue | Seller position | Buyer response |
|---|---|---|
| General warranty cap | 20% / AUD 4.8m | Reject. Start at 25% / AUD 6m. The 20% figure is only an authorised fallback, and no Amelia Frost approval has been given. |
| De minimis and basket | AUD 25,000; AUD 250,000 basket; only excess recoverable | Reject. Use AUD 5,000 de minimis and AUD 50,000 aggregate basket, with recovery from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded. |
| Claims period | 18 months | Reject. Require 24 months after Completion. The 18-month period requires Amelia Frost’s written approval, which has not been given. |
| Fundamental/title claims | Same cap and time limit as general claims | Strongly reject. Title, capacity and fundamental claims require a separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, and no general basket, de minimis or knowledge bar. |
| Fraud and misconduct | All limitations apply to all claims | Reject. Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of caps, time limits, baskets, exclusive remedies and non-reliance provisions, to the maximum extent enforceable. |
| Exclusive remedies/non-reliance | Apply to every claim | Reject. They must not restrict fraud, deliberate misconduct, fundamental/title claims or specific indemnities. |
| Disclosure | Whole data room, registers and public records disclosed | Reject. Require specific, fair disclosure identifying the relevant warranty, facts, consequences and supporting documents. Do not accept deemed disclosure from the entire data room, public registers or a “prudent search.” |
| Buyer knowledge | Bars claims based on Buyer/adviser knowledge or discoverability | Delete. Any knowledge qualifier must identify Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry. It must never apply to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. |

## Transaction-specific issues

### 1. Bluefen consent — material Completion risk

Bluefen represents approximately 30% of FY26 revenue. The disclosure expressly confirms that:

- no final written consent has been obtained; and
- there is no evidence that the conditions in clause 11.3 have been satisfied.

The Seller’s proposal to treat the matter as satisfied on delivery of consent is insufficient. Require:

- effective Bluefen consent before Completion;
- evidence that every associated condition has been satisfied;
- no consent-on-delivery mechanism; and
- a right not to complete, or an appropriate remedy, if this is not achieved.

“Reasonable endeavours” alone is inadequate for a material customer consent.

### 2. Riverlark facility and security

Approximately AUD 3.2 million remains outstanding and no final security discharge is available. A post-Completion release is unacceptable as the default position.

Require:

- a current payout figure;
- direct repayment from Completion funds;
- effective releases of all security at or before Completion; and
- if any post-Completion step is unavoidable, an irrevocable undertaking and prior written approval from Amelia Frost.

The funds flow must expressly show these payments and releases.

### 3. Employee bonuses

DD-005 identifies AUD 420,000 of conditional Completion bonuses, but the Seller confirms they are omitted from the funds flow. This is a material funds-flow and leakage issue.

Require the amount, together with triggered payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, to be:

- separately itemised in the Completion funds flow; or
- funded by the Seller without reducing the purchase price or creating an undisclosed liability for the Buyer.

The Seller must also confirm whether the conditions have been or will be triggered.

### 4. Ironquay IP

The Seller’s indemnity is too narrow because it covers only the SOW3 payment, while the contractual transfer of the Project Materials depends on payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 as open, but the disclosure says this is not independently verified.

Require a broader specific indemnity covering:

- all amounts required to secure transfer of the relevant IP;
- any failure to obtain ownership or assignment;
- third-party claims and remediation costs; and
- associated loss arising from incomplete or defective transfer.

Preserve the SOW3 cure mechanism, but do not treat the AUD 180,000 figure as verified or cap the protection to that amount without evidence.

### 5. Export/privacy incident

The Seller improperly minimises DD-006 as preliminary and immaterial. The current record involves a link sent to an unintended external address and potentially 1,240 records. It does not establish whether there was access, the full scope, notification obligations or loss.

The Buyer should not assume either that there was a confirmed breach or that there was no breach. Require:

- preservation of logs and evidence;
- a properly documented investigation;
- continuing updates before and after Completion;
- assessment of privacy, contractual and regulatory notification duties; and
- appropriate warranty/indemnity protection if the investigation identifies exposure.

No numeric claim, confirmed harm or confirmed notification duty should be conceded at this stage.

### 6. Sandbar supplier renewals

The three AUD 110,000 renewals should not automatically be treated as ordinary-course costs or Debt. The disclosure does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.

Require assessment of:

- whether the obligations are binding;
- termination rights and penalties;
- accrual and accounting treatment;
- whether they are incurred pre- or post-Completion; and
- whether any adjustment is required under the agreed debt-free/cash-free mechanics.

Do not accept an automatic Debt classification or automatic price deduction without analysis.

### 7. Tax and IP

The Seller’s assertion that tax and IP positions are “settled” is inconsistent with the Buyer’s playbook. They remain open. They must not be absorbed into the general regime without express agreement.

Maintain separate Tax, IP, payment, covenant and title protections, with no assumption of unlimited liability or resolution unless expressly approved.

### 8. Title

The DD-012 share register is merely the Seller’s identified internal source. It is not independent proof of good title, absence of encumbrances or authority to sell.

Require independent evidence of:

- ownership and title to all shares;
- absence of encumbrances;
- authority and capacity;
- constitutional and corporate approvals;
- share certificates and transfer instruments; and
- relevant independent searches or confirmations.

## Additional diligence points

The office lease and Mossvale disclosures should not be treated as harmless merely because they do not expressly say consent is required. Confirm the operative change-of-control, assignment and notification provisions, and obtain waivers or consents where required.

The Seller’s reservation clause confirms that the Buyer must evaluate the facts against the full agreement and diligence record; it does not convert the disclosed matters into accepted Buyer positions.

## Recommended negotiation priorities

1. Reinstate the 25% / AUD 6m general cap, AUD 5,000 de minimis, AUD 50,000 basket and 24-month claims period.
2. Ring-fence fundamental/title claims with a 100% cap and at least six years.
3. Carve out fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct from every limitation.
4. Replace blanket data-room/public-register disclosure and Buyer-knowledge exclusions.
5. Make Bluefen consent and satisfaction of its conditions a pre-Completion requirement.
6. Require Riverlark repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases.
7. Add the AUD 420,000 bonuses and on-costs to the funds flow or require Seller funding.
8. Expand the Ironquay indemnity and preserve the SOW3 cure.
9. Continue the DD-006 investigation with evidence preservation and reporting obligations.
10. Keep Sandbar, Tax and IP issues open pending targeted diligence.
11. Obtain independent title and encumbrance evidence rather than relying on DD-012.
=== END ADVICE ===
